subject: Recap: Quota, per-customer policies & SLA goals — Luma Analytics
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@luma.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Quota, per-customer policies & SLA goals — Luma Analytics

Hi Emma — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move to next steps.

Key pain points you shared
- High-variability customer usage: a small set of customers drive unpredictable bursts that are blowing past cost targets.
- Existing provider limits are coarse: can’t do per-customer soft/hard limits or tiered routing.
- Lack of per-customer telemetry for chargeback and billing reconciliation.

Current stack and constraints
- Core generation services run on managed endpoints from Vendor X and some self-hosted GPU pools for critical customers.
- Authentication via customer API keys; ingestion pipeline forwards requests to a central inference endpoint.
- Have strict compliance windows; SOC2 report available on request.

Success criteria for a pilot (what you told us)
- Ability to enforce per-customer rate limits (soft throttles + hard cutoffs) at API-key granularity.
- Tier-aware routing: premium customers can be routed to higher priority capacity or burst pools with SLA guarantees.
- Transparent per-customer metering (tokens, latency percentiles) for billing and SRE alerts.
- Pilot should not change existing API keys or require major client-side work.

Our proposal (high level)
- Redwood config snapshot: per-customer quota profiles (Standard / Premium / Enterprise) + global default.
- Smart routing: automatic fallback to compatible model variants when premium capacity is unavailable; optional burst pools for top N customers.
- Telemetry: token-level usage, cost estimation, and per-key latency histograms in Console (exportable to your data warehouse).
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks (2-week integration + 4-week load validation) focused on 3 customers you nominate.

Open questions / asks from your side
1) Can you share a short list (3) of high-usage customers and expected peak RPS per customer?
2) Confirm whether soft throttles (429s with informative headers) or queueing behavior is preferred for Standard tier.
3) Procurement: any required contractual templates or standard terms we should expect?
4) Please confirm if we can sign a short mutual NDA so we can exchange SOC2 and architecture diagrams.

Attachments: redwood-multitenancy-one-pager.pdf (product brief), SOW-pilot-draft-v1.docx (draft pilot scope & pricing).

Proposed next steps
- You: share customer list + procurement contact (if different from cc).
- Us: confirm pilot kickoff availability and send NDA link.
- Schedule a 30-minute follow-up to align telemetry and SLAs (I’m available Wed/Thu next week).

Thanks — looking forward to partnering.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@luma.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@luma.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Quota, per-customer policies & SLA goals — Luma Analytics

Aisha — thanks for the crisp recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications and data points attached inline below.

Customer candidates (we’ll confirm order tomorrow):
1) Bright Retail — peak ~55 req/s during sales events (avg payload ~600 tokens).
2) Nova Insights — peak ~22 req/s (longer sequences; ~1,200 tokens).
3) PilotShop (premium) — 120 req/s bursts (short 150 token calls), tends to spike unpredictably.

Preferred throttle behavior
- For Standard tier: soft throttles OR token-based rate limiting preferred; we’d like a 95th percentile headroom before hard cuts.
- For Premium: soft queueing into burst pool for short windows (<= 60s), then failover if not served.

Telemetry / Billing
- Important that token accounting aligns with our billing system. We need a deterministically reproducible token count metric (how you count subword tokens).
- We’ll need a CSV export or API to pull per-key daily aggregates for billing reconciliation.

Procurement notes
- I’m looping in Procurement. They’ll want to see SOW + security artifacts. Our standard contract template lives with Procurement (I’ll share if we get a pilot SOW).

Questions for Redwood
- Does Redwood support per-API-key routing to dedicated GPU pools without changing the request surface?
- Any native support for soft quota notifications (webhooks) for us to integrate with our rate-limit UI?

I’m comfortable with the proposed 6-week pilot; we just need the SOC2 + NDA to move internal approvals along.

—Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, Luma Analytics

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@luma.ai>, Procurement <procurement@luma.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Quota, per-customer policies & SLA goals — Luma Analytics

Great — this is super helpful, Emma. Quick answers and next actions: 

Answers
- Per-API-key routing: yes, Redwood can route requests by API key to dedicated pools (we do this via a routing policy that maps API key prefixes to capacity pools). No client-side changes required.
- Soft quota notifications: available via webhooks and Console alerts; we can push 429 hints + webhook events at pre-configured thresholds (50/75/95%).
- Token counting: we use an open tokenizer (compatible with common transformer tokenizers) and can provide the exact tokenization tool we’ll run in pilot; CSV/API exports for daily aggregates are supported.

Proposed timeline / next steps
1) I’ll send the mutual NDA DocuSign link today (see: https://docusign.net/abc123-pilot-nda). Please have that routed to Procurement.
2) Once NDA is signed, we’ll share SOC2 and an integration checklist.
3) Pilot kickoff: target week of Jun 29 — integration playbook + config template for your 3 customers.
4) Marissa will lead scoping and pricing details; Jonas will coordinate engineering onboarding.

Can you confirm procurement contact and whether Bright Retail/Nova Insights/PilotShop are fine for initial scope? If so, I’ll lock the Jun 29 kickoff and send calendar invites.

Thanks — adding a couple of attachments with finer detail on routing policy examples.

Best,
Aisha
